title: The Cold War: origins and early crises (1945–1962)
summary: Why the wartime alliance broke down, how Europe was divided, and how the Cold War spread through Korea, Hungary, Berlin and the Cuban Missile Crisis.

keyterms.definition: February 1945 meeting of Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin on Germany, Poland, the UN and Soviet entry into war with Japan.
July–August 1945 meeting of Truman, Stalin and Churchill (replaced by Attlee) where tensions over Germany and Poland grew.
US policy of preventing the spread of communism, outlined by George Kennan in 1946–47.
March 1947 pledge to support 'free peoples' resisting subjugation, starting with aid to Greece and Turkey.
US European Recovery Program (1948–52) of about $13 billion in aid to rebuild Western Europe.
Soviet closure of land routes to West Berlin (June 1948–May 1949), defeated by the Western airlift.
North Atlantic Treaty Organization, Western military alliance founded in April 1949.
Soviet-led military alliance of Eastern bloc states founded in May 1955.
Pushing a confrontation to the edge of war to force the other side to back down.
Orthodox historians blame Soviet expansion for the Cold War; revisionists stress US economic and political ambitions.
Interpretation, associated with John Lewis Gaddis, that both sides' mistrust and miscalculation shared responsibility.

questions.prompt: Put these events in chronological order.
questions.explanation: February 1945, July 1945, March 1946, March 1947, June 1948.

questions.prompt: Which issue caused the most disagreement at Yalta and Potsdam?
options: The future of Poland and Germany
questions.explanation: Stalin wanted a friendly Poland and reparations; the West wanted free elections and German recovery.

questions.text: George Kennan's 1946 'Long ___' urged firm resistance to Soviet expansion.
questions.explanation: Kennan's analysis became the basis of containment.

questions.statement: The USSR allowed Eastern European states to accept Marshall Plan aid.
questions.explanation: Stalin forbade it, seeing the plan as US economic imperialism; the Soviet response was the Molotov Plan and later Comecon (1949).

questions.prompt: What triggered the Berlin Blockade in June 1948?
options: Introduction of a new currency, the Deutschmark, in the Western zones
questions.explanation: Stalin feared a strong West German state; the airlift supplied West Berlin for nearly a year.

questions.prompt: Match each historian or school to its view.

pairs.right: Soviet expansionism caused the Cold War

questions.explanation: Soviet archives opened after 1991 shifted the debate again.

questions.text: The Western military alliance founded in April 1949 is ___.
questions.explanation: It committed members to treat an attack on one as an attack on all.

questions.prompt: Which event in 1948 convinced many in the West that Stalin intended to dominate Eastern Europe completely?
questions.explanation: The February 1948 coup ended the last democratic government in the Soviet sphere and helped pass Marshall aid in Congress.

questions.statement: The USSR tested its first atomic bomb in 1949, ending the US monopoly.
questions.explanation: Together with the communist victory in China (1949), it prompted NSC-68's call for massive rearmament.

questions.prompt: What did the Truman Doctrine first provide?
questions.explanation: Britain could no longer afford to support Greece; Truman asked Congress for $400 million.

questions.prompt: Why was the UN able to send forces to Korea in 1950?
options: The USSR was boycotting the Security Council and could not veto
questions.explanation: The Soviets were protesting that Nationalist China, not the PRC, held China's seat.

questions.prompt: Put these Korean War events in order.
questions.explanation: June 1950, September 1950, October 1950, April 1951, July 1953.

questions.statement: The Korean War ended in a peace treaty reuniting Korea.
questions.explanation: An armistice signed at Panmunjom in July 1953 left Korea divided near the 38th parallel; no peace treaty was signed.

questions.text: The Soviet-led military alliance founded in 1955 was the ___ Pact.
questions.explanation: It was formed days after West Germany joined NATO.

questions.prompt: Why did the USSR invade Hungary in November 1956?
options: Imre Nagy announced Hungary would leave the Warsaw Pact
Hungary refused to join the UN
questions.explanation: Khrushchev tolerated some reform but not withdrawal from the bloc; the West did not intervene.

questions.prompt: Match each event to its year.
questions.explanation: Khrushchev's era mixed de-Stalinisation and 'peaceful coexistence' with dangerous crises.

questions.prompt: Why was the Berlin Wall built in August 1961?
options: To stop the mass flight of East Germans to the West
To keep NATO troops out of East Berlin
As part of the Potsdam agreement
questions.explanation: Around 2.7 million had left East Germany since 1949, many of them skilled workers.

questions.text: Kennedy responded to Soviet missiles in Cuba with a naval ___ in October 1962.
questions.explanation: Calling it a quarantine avoided the legal implication of a blockade, which is an act of war.

questions.statement: As part of the Cuban Missile Crisis settlement, the USA secretly agreed to remove its missiles from Turkey.
questions.explanation: Publicly, the USA pledged not to invade Cuba; the Turkish deal was kept secret for years.

questions.prompt: Which was a consequence of the Cuban Missile Crisis?
options: A Moscow–Washington hotline (1963) and the Partial Test Ban Treaty
The immediate end of the Cold War
questions.explanation: Both leaders sought to reduce the risk of accidental nuclear war, an early step towards détente.
